articles.title: Node.js Compress and Upload AI-Generated Images to Cloud Storage: An Example Explained
articles.excerpt: The Node.js choice to compress and upload AI-generated images to cloud storage changes once the image is part of a healthtech audit trail. A receipt image is not just an asset to display later. I need…
articles.body: The Node.js choice to compress and upload AI-generated images to cloud storage changes once the image is part of a healthtech audit trail. A receipt image is not just an asset to display later. I need a small delivery object for normal processing and a trustworthy original for review. That makes compression useful, but it also makes public links, overwrite behavior, and browser delivery secondary concerns. Short answer: compress the generated image in Node.js with Sharp, upload the derived image under a deterministic key, and keep the original in a separate, access-controlled location. A storage API with a stable contract is a good fit when the application owns access decisions.

articles.title: Reply, hide, like or say nothing: how our AI comment bot decides
articles.excerpt: I'm Andrey, co-founder of Reply200, an AI comment moderation and auto-reply tool for Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube. When people hear "comment bot", they picture a script that answers everyth…
articles.body: I'm Andrey, co-founder of Reply200 , an AI comment moderation and auto-reply tool for Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube. When people hear "comment bot", they picture a script that answers everything. Writing the reply is the easy part. The hard part is deciding, for each comment, whether to answer at all. This post is about how we make that call, and what four different platform APIs forced on the design. One comment, one action Every comment gets exactly one action: reply in the page's own voice hide it like it ignore it on purpose We chose one action over "reply to everything" because replying to everything is what makes a page look automated. A fan who writes "lol" doesn't need an answer. Someone tagging a friend doesn't either. A question about shipping does.

articles.body: How I combined location-based verification and password-less authentication while building an employee attendance tracking system. Imagine you're building an attendance tracking system for a company. The objective seems straightforward: employees should be able to clock in when they arrive at the office, while administrators get a dashboard showing who's present, who's late, and how the organization is doing in terms of attendance. Simple enough, right? Well, not quite. When I started working on an attendance tracking application, I quickly realized that recording someone's arrival time was only part of the problem. I also needed to establish whether the person checking in was actually at the office and, more importantly, whether they were the employee they claimed to be.

articles.body: Draft for review · November 16, 2026 Google has opened Gemini 4 Carbon to developers through the paid Gemini API. The interesting part is not simply another “strongest model” announcement: Google is positioning Carbon as a deliberate escalation tier for long, difficult work such as multi-step debugging, large code changes, and research that benefits from repeated verification. That positioning suggests a useful engineering pattern: route ordinary requests to a faster, cheaper model, and reserve Carbon for jobs where a weak first pass or a missed edge case would cost more than additional inference. The API is straightforward; the workload is not A basic call uses the model ID gemini-4-carbon and exposes a thinking_level setting.

articles.title: MMS Meaning: What Is MMS, How It Works and Business Use
articles.excerpt: MMS means Multimedia Messaging Service. It is the phone feature that sends pictures, short videos, audio and longer text to a mobile number, with no app needed. SMS carries only short text. MMS remain…
articles.body: MMS means Multimedia Messaging Service. It is the phone feature that sends pictures, short videos, audio and longer text to a mobile number, with no app needed. SMS carries only short text. MMS remains a standard business channel in the US and Canada, while in many other markets, such as India, chat apps like WhatsApp now do much of this job. This guide explains the meaning in plain language, shows what happens when you press send, and helps you choose the right channel for your customers. Every outside fact links to its source. Note: Key takeaways MMS is a carrier service, not an app. You address a phone number, and the operators on both sides carry the message. The media doesn't travel like a text. The recipient's phone gets a short alert, then downloads the file.

articles.title: Could there be an ancient alien satellite in Earth's orbit? How the 'Black Knight' conspiracy theory has survived for over 100 years
articles.excerpt: The legend of the Black Knight satellite offers an example of how a collection of unconnected events and speculative interpretations can accumulate into a single conspiracy theory over time.
articles.body: In the final days of 1998, as astronauts aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Endeavor were working during one of the early missions to assemble the International Space Station , crew members from the STS-88 mission captured photographs of a dark colored, unusually shaped object drifting through space. Despite its unusual appearance in the photographs, the object had a conventional explanation, and one that was known to the astronauts at that time: it was one of several thermal covers that had been wrapped around trunnion pins used in the space station's construction.
